As a longtime FIFA player, I was both curious and skeptical going into *EA Sports FC 24* (let’s be honest, it’s still FIFA to all of us). After spending a good chunk of hours with it, I’d say it feels both familiar and refreshingly different, in a good way.Gameplay: There are noticeable tweaks here, especially with the new PlayStyles feature. It’s basically a rework of the old traits system, but it really does make individual players stand out more on the pitch. Now, when I’m using someone like Son, I actually feel his finesse with shots from distance. Some new mechanics, like Precision Passing, add a layer of skill to break through defenses that’s rewarding but has a learning curve.Ultimate Team: The big news is that men and women players are now combined. I didn’t expect to care, but it’s actually pretty cool to mix my favorite players from both leagues and see how they work together. The Evolutions mechanic, which lets you improve specific players over time, is also a fun addition—giving some control over stats without needing to chase special cards every week.Presentation: Graphically, the game looks as sharp as ever, with better cutscenes, reworked menus, and detailed stats overlays that make it feel even more like a real broadcast. HyperMotionV tech (if you’re on a new-gen console or PC) is pretty slick and makes movement smoother, though it’s not a game-changer on its own.What’s Missing? Career mode has some improvements, like tactical visions and coach assignments, but honestly, it still feels a bit overlooked compared to Ultimate Team. The Pro Clubs (now called "Clubs") also got a seasonal overhaul, but it’ll take a while to see if the new setup actually helps make it more engaging.Bottom Line: If you’re a long-time FIFA fan, this isn’t an overhaul, but it’s a good evolution. EA is clearly focusing on Ultimate Team, which is fine with me, but if you’re more into Career Mode or Pro Clubs, you might find it a bit less exciting. Still, it’s the best football game out there—and worth a shot, even if you’re on the fence about the rebranding.

My introduction to FIFA began with FIFA 06.I remember when my parents gave me a CD with the game, and I was overjoyed.I’d like to note that this experience significantly influenced me and shaped my attitude towards football in general. Football became a part of my life.Many years have passed since then.I wasn’t a hardcore fan of the series, but I would buy various editions of the game from time to time (08, 14, 18, 19).There were many discussions about how "Electronic Arts" was getting worse and worse. Every year, a new installment with minimal changes. Slightly improved animations, a new interface (which was often worse than the previous one).I wasn’t a fan, but I wasn’t a hater either.But with the release of FC24, I think it’s time to join the ranks of the haters.What’s wrong?FC24 is the worst entry in the series, both technically and visually.I played FIFA 19 from 2019 to 2024, and in those five years, I encountered fewer bugs than I have in less than a year of playing FC24.Here are just a few of them:the interface regularly disappears, forcing you to restart the game; players have flown into the stratosphere during matches several times; and there’s terrible optimization during corners and free kicks (did the developers, like in Cities: Skylines, decide to render every fan’s teeth?)EA holds a monopoly (PES is always a step behind) in the sports game market, and they continue to feed the audience an unfinished, underdeveloped product. One could understand their behavior, releasing a new installment every year with minimal changes. Okay, it’s a business model or something like that, but what FC24 turned out to be should never have been released. Even now, a year after the game’s launch.This is my last contribution to EA’s scam.

EA SPORTS FC™ 24 marks a significant year for the franchise, transitioning from its long-standing FIFA branding to a new era. This change has brought about a mix of anticipation and skepticism among fans and critics alike. Here's a comprehensive review of the game, focusing on various aspects that contribute to the overall experience.Gameplay and Mechanics: 4/5The core gameplay of EA SPORTS FC™ 24 remains robust, offering a familiar yet refined experience. The introduction of HyperMotion V technology and Tactical Visions has shown that the series is capable of evolving. The realistic match atmosphere, enhanced by the DualSense controller feedback, adds to the immersion, making every match feel significant.AI and Realism: 2/5Despite the advancements in gameplay, the AI still falls short of expectations. The touted improvements in artificial intelligence don't always translate into a better experience, with players occasionally making baffling decisions and goalkeepers exhibiting erratic behavior.Graphics and Environment: 5/5Graphically, EA SPORTS FC™ 24 is a feast for the eyes. The refreshed Frostbite engine delivers stunning visuals, with meticulous attention to the stadiums, players, and pitch. The volumetric data from real-life matches enhances the realism, making it one of the best-looking football games to date.Modes and Features: 3/5The game offers a variety of modes, including the popular Ultimate Team and Pro Clubs, which have received key upgrades. However, the lack of innovation in some areas, particularly in Career Modes, leaves room for improvement. The integration of women into Ultimate Team is a welcome addition, promoting inclusivity in the game.Monetization and Microtransactions: 2/5A familiar issue that continues to plague the series is the heavy focus on microtransactions, especially within the Ultimate Team mode. This aspect remains a point of contention for many players, detracting from the overall experience.Overall Note: 3.2/5EA SPORTS FC™ 24 is a mixed bag, with high points in gameplay realism and graphics but let down by AI inconsistencies and an overreliance on microtransactions. It's a step in the right direction for the series, but there's still work to be done to reach its full potential.In conclusion, EA SPORTS FC™ 24 offers a visually stunning and mechanically sound football experience that is marred by familiar issues. It's a game that will undoubtedly please fans of the series while leaving others longing for a more polished and less monetized product. The future looks promising, but for now, EA SPORTS FC™ 24 is a solid, if not groundbreaking, entry in the franchise.

Brit Tries That Football Game Series For The First TimeYou’re looking at the hours played and the ‘not recommended’ verdict and probably thinking ‘Here’s another in those series of reviews of someone whining about a game they could’ve stopped playing 80 hours ago’, and yeah, you’d be right to an extent. But my overall goal for this review/rant is to offer a first-timer's perspective into a franchise and genre that I’ve generally not paid any attention to until recently, in spite of this being the yearly obsession of much of my friend group.Contrary to popular belief, not everyone in the UK makes football their sole personality trait. I tend to tune in for the international events where England are playing, and that’s about it. And after their unfathomably lucky run to their second consecutive Euros final, I decided to give the latest FIFA a go after seeing it for an 80% off sale. And honestly, I had a lot more fun than I was expecting, though I admittedly have no other entries to compare my experience to. The gameplay is fast-paced and deep, and there are plenty of different modes to keep the experience fresh. But for a yearly franchise that should generally be aiming to improve with each iteration, EA FC 24 is a pretty embarrassing showing from most people’s favourite industry punching bag.The GoodIt shouldn’t surprise anyone that the core of FIFA is fun, but what surprised me the most is how well this was translated into options for the player on and off the pitch. The training mode helps you understand this pretty quickly; it’s not just passing, shooting, tackling and defending, it’s many types of short and long passes, different shots which prioritize either power, speed or finesse, varying mechanisms for getting the ball back with your player or bringing in an AI teammate to assist, and a staggering number of skill moves for those who really wish to master the game. It’s very easy to learn FIFA, but I wasn’t anywhere near close to fully understanding it by the end of my playtime.The above does not consider the additional layer of strategy that comes with the formations and player instructions, giving each squad you build a far more noticeably distinct identity than I was expecting. Finding the ideal formation for your playstyle will already promote a lot of experimentation, and adding defensive and offensive tactics on top of this will change its feel even further. What’s great about this system is you can build multiple custom tactics and switch them on the fly during a game. Player instructions are probably the most noticeable tactic you can manipulate, as telling your forwards to either run behind the opposition if they’re particularly pacey, or stand outside of the box if they have good long-range shot capabilities, can completely change how effective their best attributes are. So, understanding your team on an individual and group level is interesting to navigate and exploit.And I am also pleased with the number of different modes on offer, which helps add plentiful value and replayability. Ultimate Team is the reason most people buy into this, and I’m happy to report that building up a strong squad for free is quite doable in good time nowadays. Player and Manager Career mode gives you two different perspectives on a longer-term football journey, Clubs are the more skill-based PVP experience, and Volta is completely different to any of the above, with a smaller team size, faster pace and skill moves being the primary changes here. This was probably the mode where I had the most consistent fun since it encourages team play on a small scale, and I scored and assisted many great goals when I was matched with collaborative teammates.Now we get onto the numerous parts of FC 24 that irritated me. There’s no ‘Bad’ section here as these issues affect fundamental aspects of the experience which really should not be an issue considering we are more than 20 versions deep into this franchise. So areas like bugs really should not be an issue, especially when it comes to menus, of which there were surprisingly numerous. Simply navigating these would softlock me on average once per day, forcing me to restart and wait for EA’s launcher to actually boot up the game again, as there were some cases where it just forgot to do so. I even managed to find a ‘Debug’ menu option on one occasion, and I could not tell you what I was doing that allowed me to get there in the first place. I also experienced many visual UI bugs particularly when viewing my Ultimate Team Squads, and certain UI elements would appear and disappear seemingly at random when in-game.Focusing more on Ultimate Team, I am staggered that there were consistent server problems even during off-peak times. I’ve had zero issues with online multiplayer after upgrading my internet, and FC 24 is the only game since then where I would be randomly put on high ping or even disconnected from my opponent for no good reason. And of course, being kicked out or losing a match due to poor latency will affect both your Rivals progress and expend your team’s contracts, so it’s a gigantic waste of time that you can’t do anything about. There were also many occasions where the command I gave to a player would either not connect with the power or direction that I intended, or would simply not respond to any command at all, typically leading to possession loss during a crucial moment. This never once happened when I played offline, so I suspect EA’s netcode is in dire need of reconstruction, as a game demanding consistent accuracy from the player needs to respond perfectly on every occasion.You know how I praised all of the tactical options the game gives you? Throw all of that out of the window for Rivals as there are a few meta combinations which are guaranteed to wipe the floor with your squad if you aren’t also using a meta setup. It was really lame to have match after match with my opponent running a single forward who the ball would be lobbed to while my defence was a decent way up the pitch, leading to them scoring before I could do anything about it. The saying goes to not hate the player but the game, and so the fact that EA has allowed such tactics to work when they would never fly in a real match is really odd.And finally, the grind was particularly grim for both the Ultimate Team season and Volta cosmetic unlocks. Progression is largely built around being time-gated, where playing outside of periods when there aren’t specific challenges available will result in essentially meagre exp gain, meaning the game largely discourages you from playing it much of the time. And even when there are challenges available, the most reliable way to earn them is in squad battles, and they get very repetitive since the AI there is not challenging to play against. As for Volta, earning a single cosmetic takes dozens upon dozens of successful matches to get a simple reskin, and so earning those 50 vanity items for one achievement is a gigantic pain. But obviously, you can pay to skip the grind if you wish…Nah. Or at least, definitely not at full price. I will give EA credit that this was an interesting diversion from the type of games I’m used to playing, and the 100% achievements journey I went on was pretty entertaining for the most part. But after dealing with numerous UI and server issues, inconsistent controls, unbalanced multiplayer and some incredibly grindy progression, I can’t see myself putting 100 more hours in to knock out another 100% without getting frustrated or bored along the way. The earliest I can see myself checking back is in two summers’ time at an 80% discount when the next World Cup rolls around; but only if England get anywhere, of course.

EA FC 24 is a huge step back from FIFA 23. The game is sluggish, more exploitative, not fun at all. So many things are broken.Tackling...too easy, ball is constantly changing possession every two seconds. In real football, defenders hold back in respect, so on-ball players have time with the ball at their feet. In this game, you have to spam pass just to avoid onslaught of spam tackling.Dribbling....due to ease of spam tackling, pushing, shirt tugging, you have to constantly excessively finesse dribble - slow then fast, forward then back, left then right, over and over, just to move the ball down the pitch. It's incredibly annoying and causes migraines.Play Styles ...contradict player ratings. A top overall player ratings-wise excelled at a range of things. But now, without certain play style abilities, they're dumbed down in those facets of play, while worse players with those Play Style abilities are better at those facets. I understand the idea to individualize players, but player ratings on their own worked better. EA would've been better off adding new attributes like Arial, Block, Travella, etc, instead of creating Play Styles. Ratings allows for separation of skills between best and worst players, whereas abilities you either have it or not.Passing....to add to the ordeal of the tackling and constant possession change, too many passes are intercepted, blocked, ricochet, or go wide of their target. All because to push the Precision Passing mechanics, which in itself isn't reliable or something you can use as a replacement to regular passing.Player Positioning ...goalkeepers are worse than before, too often out of position or useless. Attacking players in the box are worse than before, too stationary or don't get into space. Crosses or cutbacks often don't go to them at all, again to promote use of Precision Passing mechanics.Mechanics...the game is bogged down with mechanics, old and new mechanics. Too much emphasis on that...precision passing, skill moves, hypermotion, tactical defending, play styles, etc etc. Too many unstable moving parts, this isn't a Swiss watch.Overall, it's a wretched experience. The free-flowing, free-wheeling nature of FIFA 23 is gone. F23 had its flaws, not like real football, but FC24 has gone the other way, trying to be too tactical, structured, and confined that it also isn't like real football. Neither is like real football, but FC24 is an ordeal. F23 at least you could enjoy it.Remember, real football is fun to play. It's free-flowing. Players don't charge into you constantly tackling, pushing, pulling and diving. They hold their ground, compress.Future patches....focus on nerfing tackling, instead emphasizing jockeying and sealing, the defense and capable AI compressing space. Players should have time with the ball at their feet, play is free-flowing, but they have to find a way around or thru a compressing defense, rather than being met with an onslaught of charging defenders rough-housing them up and down the pitch. Not a game of constant turnovers from rough tackles, but a game of doing something creative with your opportunity with the ball across an equal share of possession.

Here’s my in-depth take on what’s working and what’s not.Positives:Gameplay Realism: EA Sports FC 24 has taken strides toward realism, especially with its updated physics engine and HyperMotion V technology. Player movements, ball physics, and overall match flow feel more authentic, making every goal and defensive play that much more satisfying. This realism, while appealing, does raise the skill ceiling, requiring players to be more deliberate with their actions on the pitch.Quality of Life Improvements: Off the field, EA has made significant changes that streamline navigation and management tasks. Whether it's the new menu system in Ultimate Team or the ability to upgrade player cards with the Evolutions feature, these enhancements make the grind feel less cumbersome and more engaging. The addition of crossplay in Clubs mode is also a huge win, increasing accessibility and competition.Career Mode Depth: For those who enjoy single-player modes, the enhancements in Career Mode are noteworthy. The Tactical Vision feature and the ability to hire coaching staff add layers of depth that bring a more immersive RPG-like experience to managing your team. These changes help make Career Mode feel fresh and engaging, even after many hours.Negatives:Gameplay Pacing and Defending Issues: While realism is a strength, it also comes with some drawbacks. The slower pace of the game can feel sluggish, especially when defending. AI defenders often feel unresponsive or too slow to react, leading to frustrating situations where attackers can easily bypass them. This is compounded by issues with goalkeeper behavior, where they frequently fail at basic saves, leading to goals that feel unfair.Bugs and Glitches: Unfortunately, EA Sports FC 24 is plagued with a fair share of bugs. These range from minor visual glitches to more serious issues like broken matchmaking in Pro Clubs and oddities in Career Mode negotiations. The bugs are frequent enough to detract from the overall experience and remind players of the game’s unfinished edges.Ultimate Team’s Monetization: Ultimate Team remains the centerpiece of EA’s sports games, and while it’s packed with content, it’s also more pay-to-win than ever. The introduction of female players and new squad-building options are great, but the heavy emphasis on microtransactions can make it feel like your success is tied more to your wallet than your skill.Verdict:EA Sports FC 24 is a game with high highs and frustrating lows. It’s a step forward in terms of realism and depth, especially in Career Mode, but issues with gameplay pacing, defending, and the ever-present bugs hold it back from being truly great. If you’re a longtime fan of the series, you’ll find a lot to enjoy, but be prepared for moments of frustration along the way. Overall, it’s a solid entry that could benefit from some post-launch updates to address its more glaring issues.

If you thought EA's yearly cash grab couldn't get any worse, EA FC 24 proves that they can still find new ways to disappoint their fanbase. As a long-time fan of the FIFA series, transitioning to EA FC 24 on PC has been nothing short of a nightmare. This game is a glaring example of how little EA cares about the quality of their product, especially for PC gamers.Performance Issues & Bugs:From the moment you launch the game, you’re greeted with a host of performance issues that make it nearly unplayable. The optimization is atrocious, even on high-end systems. Stuttering, frame drops, and crashes are far too common. It’s baffling how a company with EA's resources can release such a poorly optimized game. But it doesn't stop there—there are widespread reports of bugs that break the game entirely. Some players can’t even get past the main menu without experiencing crashes. Others have seen bizarre glitches, like players disappearing on the pitch or the ball passing through goalkeepers as if they were ghosts.Gameplay Mechanics:When the game actually runs, you’ll wish it hadn’t. The gameplay is clunky and feels like a massive step back from previous iterations. Passes are erratic, the AI is brain-dead, and the much-hyped new features barely function as intended. The physics engine seems to have regressed, with ridiculous ball physics and unrealistic player movements that make the game feel more like a bad arcade title than a football simulation.User Interface & Online Issues:The user interface is another point of frustration. It’s sluggish, unintuitive, and riddled with delays. But the worst part is the online experience. Matchmaking is broken, leading to frequent disconnects, lag, and input delays that ruin any competitive match. Playing Ultimate Team feels like you’re fighting the game’s infrastructure as much as your opponent.Microtransactions & Pay-to-Win:And of course, no EA game would be complete without predatory microtransactions. EA FC 24 continues the trend of locking the best content behind paywalls, pushing players towards spending real money on Ultimate Team packs to remain competitive. This blatant pay-to-win model is infuriating, especially when paired with the game’s fundamental flaws. Why should anyone pay extra for a game that can’t even run properly?Community Feedback Ignored:EA’s response to these issues has been lackluster, to say the least. Despite the outcry from the community, they’ve done little to address the glaring problems with the PC version. Patches are slow to arrive and often fail to fix the most critical issues, leaving players stuck with a broken game.Final Verdict:In its current state, EA FC 24 is not worth your time or money, especially on PC. It’s a half-baked, glitch-ridden mess that prioritizes squeezing money from players over delivering a quality football experience. Until EA makes serious improvements—and stops treating their player base as an ATM—this game is best avoided.Save your money and sanity. There are better ways to enjoy football than this frustrating excuse for a game.

DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. DO NOT EVEN BUY THIS GAME ON SALE. To put it simply, this game is a broken piece of garbage. I have about 348 hours in this diabolical game so I fee like I know what I'm talking about. I genuinely feel like I contracted some kind of disease from EA FC 24. Now, I tried my best to play at least once of every game mode in this game so I will go in depth about what I experienced.Pro Clubs - This game mode can be fun with friends. The way you level up is by playing well throughout the game so in some way in gives you an incentive to actually do well. If you play like crap, you won't get as much xp. Playing with randoms can be a hit or miss, I have come across genuine players who play smart like making good timely passes and taking smart shots. On the other hand, occasionally I have come across a player or two who will just like to troll. For example, if they play a GK they will intentionally come out of the net and play up the field leaving the goal wide open for your opponents to easily score. You can also make your own club for your friends to join and compete with other clubs but I can't say a whole lot on that since I haven't played much of it.Volta - Now with Volta this game mode can be fun but the execution could have done way better. There's no story or anything, you just create your character, choose a special ability, and dive into a game. Now the special abilities is where I have problem when it comes to Volta. You can choose four abilities: power shot, speed, strength, and aerial. The power shot grants you the ability to shoot from anywhere in the pitch with unhuman like power and is almost a guaranteed goal. The speed ability you basically become The Flash for a few seconds. Strength ability, when activated you can knock over any opponent. Aerial, you can literally jump towards the ceiling and score easy header goals. All the special abilities that I just mentioned really takes the fun out of Volta. People abuse these abilities and it's not so much about skills and fancy tricks like how it should be like in Fifa Street.Ultimate Team - Don't even touch this game mode. Only thing that's new is that they added women cards that can be played with the men. Overall, this game mode is very much still a cash-grabbing scam I would strongly recommend to avoid at all costs.Career Mode - Career mode is I think actually quite nice. There are some cinematic scenes which I enjoy as it makes the game feel more lively. You can start off an big club like Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, or Man City or you can choose to start off at a lower tier league and work your way up towards the bigger clubs. I personally choose starting at a lower tier league for realism and you play more. There are usually three objectives that you are given as you play that you have to try and complete. If you compete them your manager likes it and his approval rating for you gets higher. There is also some side activities that you can do during your free-time in Career mode like go on vacation with family or friends or invest in the stoke market. It doesn't show your player actually doing any kind of activity which is downside. Depending on what you choose, it does however help your personality. Personality is 3 types you can choose from. Heartbeat, Virtuoso, and Maverick. Each has their own benefits and perks you can obtain to help your playstyle.Manager Mode - With this mode I think it's fun. For the most part, everyone has a real face except for managers who play in the lower leagues. You can also create your own character and manage a real-life club or you can make your own. I made my own started off in the English League two and worked my way up the Premier League which I had a lot of fun doing. You can do basically what a real-life manager would do like make transfers, choose tactics, sign head training coaches to help the system you want to implement at your club, etc.Seasons, Co-Op seasons - Honestly haven't played these game modes as I have no friends to play this with so I can't give an in-depth review.Game mechanics - In terms of gameplay, it just seems like just a round of pass, pass, pass, pass, ball ricochet off opponent, opponent has ball now, pass, pass, pass, miss challenge or foul, pass, pass, score. It gets repetitive really fast and quite boring. When I played clubs, all my opponents would have to do is if they are fast enough, just run to the outter edges of the penalty box near the goalpost, cross it into the center, and 9 times out of ten there would be someone waiting for that cross and it's an easy score. It takes ZERO skill to do this and very easily abused. Defending it pretty much non-existent in this game. The ball just going to ricochet off either you or somebody on the your team and any kind of challenge even if you think it's a good one, it's almost guaranteed a foul.Summary - Overall, despite some of the positives I mentioned EA FC 24 is a half baked mess of a game. EA have no competition when it comes to making football games so they aren't even going to try because they know that fans will buy their game anyway. This is last football game I will play from EA. Don't waste your time or energy playing this game, it's not worth it.

gregor's ea fc 24 review:PART 1: different timesLike many children growing up during the 2000s, I made my first experiences with football video games early in life. Surprisingly enough it wasn't Fifa though, but its, back then much more than now, competitor Pro Evolution Soccer. Playing on the Playstation 2 one of my friends owned back in the day, when I was a Nintendo kid myself, PES was something completely new. And I was immediately sold. We would simply play exhibition matches versus the ai, one of us the first half, the other the second half of the match. We would only use one controller for some reason. The ai would be set to the lowest difficulty and we would win 15-0 every match. Never felt like raising the difficulty, never felt like changing anything at all. What followed was me getting into PES myself. Playing some on PC, some on Nintendo DS and at some point playing on the Wii. And that is where I did the unthinkable. I dared to change something, much to the disliking of my friend. I convinced my mom to get me Fifa. Everything I enjoyed in PES, I enjoyed more in Fifa. Getting older and therefore understanding more about the game I got into all the gamemodes. Career mode was what got me to stick. The following years Fifa was always a part of my life. Playing on Wii, Wiiu and eventually Playstation 4 and 5. Grinding Ultimate Team. Complaining about missing features in career mode. And most of all raging at the imperfect gameplay. Spending thousands of hours on the game. And here we are today. Fifa is no more. EA Fc 24.PART 2: a new worldSo, EA Fc 24 it is. Launching the game for the first time, I had a strange feeling. This just wasn't something the Fifa player was used to. Things being so different. The name changing might seem trivial to some. Meaningless even. But it challenged the Fifa player in a way that no other Fifa game ever did. It introduces itself as change. The one thing no Fifa game ever does. Change. So from the title card, you immediately experience something new. A whole new vibe. "Pressing a button" to start the game feels like playing PES with my friend back in the day again. Not knowing what to expect. Not knowing what is to come. An excitement that was lost during all the years of Fifa. Experiencing everything in the game without any familiarity again. Every menu, every skill move, every goal and every gamemode. It all feels fresh again. Like there is something to be discovered. By you.PART 3: overstimulationAnd so discover I did. Going straight in: career mode! My old love. So many ideas at an instance: play with my favorite team, start from the lowest division with the worst team, try to win everyting, a journey man save, play as a real manager and so on... What is great about this game is that, even though it does not feel like Fifa, it still feels intuitive to the football fan. The menus can be navigated instinctively. There is no time spent wondering how to use the game. Navigating the game, using its plethora of functions does not feel restrictive. You can finally fly again, after being drowned in Fifa's mediocrity for so many years. Next, let's play some Ultimate Team. FUT is no longer, just UT. Reestablishing the name change. Everything I felt in career mode, I felt ten times in UT. What a rush to start building your team. In Fifa this often felt pointless to me, knowing that all progress would be wiped by next year, having to start once more. Doing this over and over in Fifa. But now we are EA Fc 24. The experience is vibrant. A colourful joy. With something to do and achieve for everybody.PART 4: technicalitiesSadly we have arrived. We have arrived at the point, where the past catches up to our hype train of ecstasy. I would have loved to rejoice in the homogenous mixture of childhood nostalgia and the urge to explore this game puts you through, but it seems as though such things can never last. And the gameplay is where this game falls short of its own ambitions. When you put in the hours, grinding the game, playing match after match, this is where the paint cracks. You begin to notice one inevitable truth. This isn't an entirely new game. Under the new paint on all the walls lies its unforgiving demise. Fifa. The L1 elasticos are still there. The auto defending is still there. The pace meta is still there. The rats are still ratting away, moving their goalkeepers and taking 15 minutes for their corners. And once you start noticing one of those cracks, the whole card house that is EA Fc 24 collapses.PART 5: cataclysmWhat could have been so much, should have been so much and wanted to be so much, ended up being too little. Ended up doing more damage than any of its predecessors. The game's greatest asset is also what makes it the most disappointing entry in the long line of EA football games. The promise of change, announced in the very title, ends up a broken promise. The player in despair. Giving EA one last chance on the game that finally suggests awareness. But it is a lie. EA Fc 24 is a lie. The game truly is Fifa 24 in disguise. And Fifa 24 we did not want.

This game is a complete and utter embarrassment to the EA franchise. I have been playing FIFA since 05 on a GameCube console (since 2013 online) and have admired how greatly the game has developed over the years. Out of all sports games such as Madden, NBA2K, NHL, PES, and others, FIFA’s game mechanics have always been the most precise and better developed in my opinion. However, during the last 2 releases the game has taken a terrible dip. This game genuinely feels uncontrollable.-Player movement: Who cares if you’re running with Mbappe or Haaland on an offensive breakthrough; what would’ve been an almost certain goal on previous games now feels like an opportunity for the game to screw you over by having a no name defender catching up and tugging on your forward or blocking your shot. Players feel stiff, uncontrollable, and slow. The skill movements we once got to enjoy now are incredibly slow and useless.- Passing: The passing has been incredibly inconsistent. Wether it is the direction or power behind the pass, you do not get the results of the pass you’re intending to make often turning the ball over to the other team or passing it to the wrong teamate. The through passes are very inconsistent as well, often going straight to the defender as opposed to ahead of a running forward. Crosses to the box are also very inconsistent, I’ll just leave that one at that.- AI off-ball movement: I don’t even know where to begin with this, it seems like EA relied on a diversity hire to program this. Defensively, the game will pack the box whenever you reach the other team’s defensive third making it nearly impossible to make a pass or to take a shot regardless of how much you pass the ball to open up a space. You seriously have to rely on running in short circles with one player to get any chance of shooting. However, on a counter attack, who knows what is going on because you can literally just kick the ball from your defensive end and somehow get a 3v1 against the other team because their defenders are nowhere to be found.Offensively, AI players will stop running to the box to receive a cross or a through pass often sticking to the defender or just slowing down entirely instead of getting open for a header or shot. I won’t even talk about the goalkeepers, I’ve seen e ouch people write about them.- Shooting: Forget about curved shots from outside the box, it is incredible how high ranked forwards and midfielders will just completely shank these type of shots or shoot them at such a slow speed that it almost looks like a lob. Only a handful of players can take descent shots from outside the box. The direction and power behind shots are also inconsistent. Once again, inconsistency.- Defense: This probably stresses me out the most. Just because you stab the ball of the other player does not even come close to a guarantee that you will gain possession. The worst is when you find yourself in a 1 on 1 situation against a forward and you stab the ball and bounces off the forward towards your goal giving him an open shot. In the midfield, when this happens, it just turns into utter chaos and no one can keep control of the ball to save their lives. The defensive players also are hard to control and move accurately so unfortunately it is better a lot of time to just rely on the AI to do the work making the game less enjoyable.

I don't want to change their training schedules individually for each player, daily....wtf....who asked for this... The game says just do it monthly, but then will keep popping up with emails saying so-in-so is super exhausted, check out his training (and that email comes in bugged too...lol...the levels of incompetence are high). So, IDK, maybe I won't be simming seasons either.

The game strikes a perfect balance between realism and fun, ensuring that each match is both challenging and enjoyable. With its polished mechanics, breathtaking graphics, and robust game modes, FIFA 24 sets a new standard for sports simulations.In conclusion, FIFA 24 isn't just an incremental upgrade; it's a significant leap forward that redefines the virtual football experience. There are mandatory stutters and drops throughout the game, and I am not exaggerating. If you have played previous games, you know that replays, in-game cutscenes, or transitions happen frequently. Every time you score a goal, make a foul, or during match intros, there will be transitions or replays, causing stutters and FPS drops during these events. Oh Fifa, how I love you. Oh wait, no, sorry, EA FC 24. Or EA SPORTS FC 24. Have we as a community yet decided on what to unofficially call this? Fifa rolls off the tongue, but it's not right, and the new title is as about as appealing as calling Reading FC 'the biscuit men'.But I digress.This has started out as the worst iteration of the series; for both specific reasons, and the reason of... it just is. It just feels heavy, and nasty. The tackling feels wacky and broken, especially standing tackle for the user. Then again, the CPU get's on just fine with this. Half of the tackles I make, the CPU get's the ball back as my player cannot be bothered to chase it. The ball becomes glued to the CPUs legs when they tackle me.Is this a skill issue? Probably. But not one I've ever had to worry about. I apparently do now, however.On the subject of chasing the ball, you remember in old Fifa games, you'd constantly be screaming at your player while they're full sprinting for a ball you know will go out of bounds, wasting the precious second wind energy in the 79th minute? Yeah, that's not a thing anymore. Your player will just stand there. You'll actually start to miss that infuriating mechanic.The UI is awful. Quick access buttons have been removed and replaced with things no one needs. Take career mode. You wanna hit X (or square) to quicksave? Haha well, get yourself scrolling all the way to the right in this laggy menu. Wanna view the calendar with the right thumbstick? Nah you don't, you want to view your notifications (which on old Fifas was bound to the left thumbstick. They've just moved it and not bothered rebinding the other one).And the performance. Woof. Let me clear something up; I very much dislike those who moan about FPS and then proceed to list off their specs. It irks me. Grinds my gears. However! Just this once I will say this: my PCs specs would laugh at the recommended specs on the playground. I still get FPS drops quite regularly, even on lowered settings. The menu has more delay than a deaf person reacting to the start pistol of a 100m sprint.Conclusion? Get the game if you want the new kits, new teams, new everything from the past season, which has now finished. But if you haven't already bought it, give it a miss, carry on playing a previous version and wait for the next one. Maybe it'll be better; maybe it'll be worse. You'd think how could it be worse, but somehow 2K manage it every year with NBA. Otherwise do what I did. Get EA Play and play it for a few hours.Happy gaming.

I love Fifa games, but I cannot recommend FC 24 on PC.It's pretty poorly optimised. Some examples:Ultrawide users are hardcapped to 60FPS, but the game never tells you this, sending you down a rabbit hole of troubleshooting for nothing.You cannot have uncapped framerate in fullscreen mode (otherwise you're limited to max 144fps). Again, the game does not tell you this.Glitches, crashes, performance issues, and other bad PC-port symptoms are all here. My game has frozen on a couple of occasions when going into the half-time menu, once in a single player mode (I lost all unsaved progress, luckly the game autosaves) and a couple of times in an online multiplayer match (which presumably penalises you with a DNF in matchmaking).For the first few months after release, there was constant choppiness and stuttering during in-game cut-scenes (such as the ref talking to players, opening animations, etc). It was eventually fixed but I have to stress it was months before resolution.You'll buy the game on Steam, but it actually runs and launches off the EA games launcher, similar to Ubisoft games. This is mostly not an issue, but if the EA launcher ever glitches out or has any issues, you won't be able to play your game until you fix whatever's wrong with the EA app. This has only happened to me once, but be aware.And by far, the MOST frustrating, infuriating, EA-like issue ever: if you ever use your mouse and keyboard to select ANYTHING in the menus, you run a risk of being forced to use M+KB as your controller when in-game, EVEN IF you have a gamepad connected. The game gives you NO WAY of changing your controller mid-game. I've had to forfeit rivals games and restart career mnode games because I was locked into using the keyboard.You would think having access to the mouse would be a benefit - it makes organising your career mode and ultimate team much easier and faster, but it instead sets you up to have to quit and restart your game. I honestly believe that if any dev at EA played their own game on PC, this ridiculous oversight would have been caught much earlier.This isn't a fault of the PC version, but Clubs and Ultimate Team are the only game-modes where you will match-make with anyone reliably - sadly, this affects my beloved Volta mode, which I have only played 1 online match in so far. And given that this is largely a console game, most your opponents are playing on consoles with Wifi connections, meaning you will often have connection issues.PC Ultimate team players are locked into their own transfer market, while console players have a big shared market. This means fewer items at higher prices. This is disappointing, but understandable, given that it's a measure to combat cheaters and prevent bots and coin farmers from ruining the transfer economy.Further, as always with Fifa games, a lot of the playerbase are generally quite nasty and negative and tend to hate everything about the game at all times (see the most popular review on steam for an example), but this is nothing new.It's a bit disappointing, but it is what it is.If you can get past all those issues, FC24 is actually the most well-polished iteration so far. If you're not on ultrawide, playing this game at 2K or 4k 160hz is actually an awesomely smooth and fluid experience, and is the best way to play the game. Or if you ARE on a ludicrously giant ultrawide, you you can tweak your camera settings to get a full-view of the entire pitch, which looks awesome but I haven't tried it. Regardless, the point is that you get a unique and improved experience over what a console can provide (but also lots of unique bugs).The new playstyles mechanics make the game engaging in every mode I've tried - ultimate team, career and clubs, and it gives you a new angle to evaluate and develop players. Having to make a difficult choice between two very good options makes your decisions more meaningful and gratifying.Further, Ultimate team has changed a lot since I last played (Fifa21), for the better. Whereas before, you would eke out what you could with Gold players, this game is more than happy to give you strong and high-rarity cards quite freely if you engage with its mechanics. Further, the new evolutions mechanic is very satisfying, as it allows you to upgrade players you have for free. In some instances, you can upgrade regular gold or silver players to be very powerful cards indeed.The game is actually reasonably mechanically demanding if you can master the elusive timed-finishes. For the most part, patient defence, intelligent attack and good gamesense will win you more games than just having better players. Tactic adjustments change your team-mates AI movements in a meaningful way and is fun to experiment with.There are a lot of problems with FC24 on PC, and if you can, I'd recommend getting this game on console with a 120hz monitor (I believe PS5 and Series X can do 4k@120 with this game). As far as the PC port goes, I can only recommend this to the very patient or masochistic.

As an avid follower of the FIFA franchise, delving into the latest installment, FIFA 24, felt like stepping onto a freshly laid pitch under the floodlights of a packed stadium. Developed by EA Sports, this iteration of the beloved football simulation game promises to redefine the virtual football experience, and it certainly delivers on that promise.Graphically, FIFA 24 is a feast for the eyes. Player models are incredibly detailed, from the sweat glistening on their brows to the grass stains on their kits. The stadiums are breathtakingly realistic, capturing the essence of iconic venues from around the world. Whether you're playing under the electric atmosphere of Anfield or the sun-drenched pitch of the Maracanã, each location feels alive and immersive.But visuals are just the tip of the iceberg. FIFA 24 introduces groundbreaking gameplay features that elevate the series to new heights. The enhanced ball physics make every pass, shot, and tackle feel more lifelike than ever before. The revamped AI ensures that each match is filled with dynamic and unpredictable moments, keeping you on the edge of your seat until the final whistle blows.One of the standout features of FIFA 24 is the Career Mode, which has undergone a major overhaul. Now, you have more control over every aspect of your team, from training regimes to transfer negotiations. The addition of player personalities adds another layer of depth, making each player feel unique and adding an extra challenge to team management.Of course, no FIFA game would be complete without its signature multiplayer modes, and FIFA 24 delivers in spades. Whether you're competing against friends in local matches or testing your skills against players from around the world in online seasons, there's no shortage of ways to enjoy the beautiful game with others.However, FIFA 24 isn't without its flaws. Some may find the learning curve steep, especially newcomers to the series or casual players. And while the inclusion of microtransactions is nothing new, some may feel that they're more intrusive than in previous iterations.Overall, FIFA 24 is a triumph of virtual football. With stunning visuals, innovative gameplay mechanics, and a wealth of content to keep players coming back for more, it's a must-have for any fan of the beautiful game. Whether you're a seasoned veteran or a newcomer to the series, FIFA 24 offers an experience that's as exhilarating as scoring a last-minute winner in the Champions League final.

Had it not gone 70% off in a sale, there would genuinely be 0 reason for a rational person to purchase this game. Even now I find it hard to justify buying this game with 70% off.Somehow they have managed to make a game-mode which might as well not exist in their eyes worse. Career mode has gotten little to no change outside of questionable UI-changes in the past few years. And yet they have made it worse than last years edition.The gameplay compared to past years feel significantly worse, against AI you have old issues which have not been resolved like midfielders not tracking back to defend. Online against other players, you better pray to god before your game starts that your players haven't been replaced with lookalikes from a retirement home. One game you can have something that could represent a decent implementation of a football game, the next game you are controlling a football team who decided to play with ice-skates, and have been played in an rink.I doubt that the AI has changed much, but the way in which it has been programmed, has led to cheesy tactics such as switching play by crossing it across field because your defender on the opposite flank decided that the opponent deserves a free run at the wing.This issue is compounded by the fact that EA has made it impossible to play through the middle, even if playing through the middle is significantly more difficult in real life, that does not justify the opposition striker nailing a perfect standing tackle from behind on my midfielder running full steam away from him.Corners are also victim to cheese tactics, now people just bring their keepers out and there's nothing you can do, unless you curve it precisely into the goal, or give a good delivery to unfavorable spots on the near or far post, the only option to not needlessly lose the ball is to play it short.Which opens up another stupid avenue of attacking, after playing it short you get the option to just cross it to the back post from the half-space at the edge of the box, and you'd miraculously get a free header.Even basically mechanics such as shooting and passing is victim to the whims of EAs horrible game, in one game you can score every other shot, and yet you can load into the next match and your player decided that he was Nicholas Jackson.Passing, there's 2 issues with passing, first we have the animation for your player to actually take a pass, sometimes your player can pass like a normal human being, with leg movement like you'd expect, the next moment you'd think that a ghost was hugging his foot based on how long it takes for him to actually take the pass. You could put a pass with 2/4 bars so that its fast enough to reach your player, but not too fast where he can't control it, end up as a misplaced pass with no speed that according to passing AI, was meant for the player behind my intended pass target.Oh and its usual business with defending.

FC24, the long-standing franchise for football enthusiasts, returns once more to the pitch with its latest installment. While it remains the most accurate simulation of the sport available, its failure to introduce substantial new features leaves much to be desired.Pros:Authenticity: FC24 continues to excel in replicating the real-life essence of football, from player movements to stadium atmosphere.Gameplay Mechanics: The core mechanics of the game remain solid, providing an engaging and realistic football experience for players.Cons:Stagnation: Despite being a reliable choice for football gaming, FC24 suffers from a lack of innovation. The absence of significant new features makes each installment feel repetitive and fails to justify the purchase for returning players.Neglect of Manager Career Mode: The franchise's emphasis on Ultimate Team mode has overshadowed the Manager Career mode, leaving it relatively untouched in terms of innovation. Introducing features like sponsorships and customizable kits could breathe new life into this mode and enhance the overall experience for players seeking managerial immersion.Limited Customization: While FC24 offers some customization options, they remain relatively basic compared to other modern sports games. Adding deeper customization features for kits, stadiums, and player appearance would greatly enhance player engagement and personalization.Verdict:FC24 remains a solid choice for football gaming enthusiasts who prioritize realism and accuracy. However, its failure to innovate significantly hampers its appeal, especially for long-time fans who crave fresh experiences with each iteration. With a renewed focus on introducing meaningful features, particularly in Manager Career mode, FC24 has the potential to reclaim its position as the ultimate football simulation game. Until then, it falls short of reaching its full potential.

This game has Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment for multiplayer games! (DDA) is essentially about tweaking the AI's challenge level. It operates across five tiers: Amateur, semi-pro, professional, world class, and legendary. EA determines a human player's rating by analyzing various stats like wins, losses, goals scored, goals conceded, and more. They then assign a skill level rating to that player accordingly. For instance, in an online match, if a semi-pro player is pitted against a world-class player due to matchmaking issues, DDA comes into play.Upon recognizing the skill gap, DDA aims to "balance" the match. The world-class player's AI is downgraded to semi-pro (though the player doesn't notice because the change is done in secret inside the GAME CODE) while the semi-pro player's AI is upgraded to world class. Essentially, when the semi-pro player attacks, the AI defense matches their level to maintain a "competitive experience". Conversely, when the world-class player attacks, the AI defense rises to their level to prevent an easy victory against the semi-pro opponent.There is a very simple way to prove this without the shadow of a doubt, but it involves loosing on purpose and becoming very bad yourself in competitive matches. There's obviously no issue with my connection to cause so much trouble but basically I have to re-launch the game 2-3 times every time to get it to connect to the internet. I tried asking for help in the EA forums but to no avail. So I suspect these issues are widely known but they are not getting fixed for months now.In terms of gameplay, it's not that bad, but it's the same formula EA FC and FIFA have been using for years. It's essentially the same game compared to what it was last year. Notably, defense feels odd and inconsistent, and there are some balance issues (ie controlled sprint, or whatever that dribbling technique is called, is overpowered).Finally, I'll also address the elephant in the room. I haven't played an EA game for years. But I got that football nostalgia and I bought this year's edition. I was amazed seeing the way they promote EA points. For instance, you can get an evolution for 1000 points or a staggering 300.000 gold (the numbers are not exactly right but you get my point). So the comparative worth of those 2 (bought points and earned points) does not seem balanced.Those are my 2 cents. I played the game extensively so you don't have to.TL;DR* Too many bugs on PC* Indirectly pay-to-win* Gameplay is not that bad but I don't think there are major changes compared to previous versions

Title: "Mixed Bag of Brilliance and Bugs"Rating: ⭐⭐½Pros:EA FC Sports 24 delivers a visually stunning experience with its awesome graphics, making every match feel like a cinematic spectacle. Coupled with a great soundtrack that amps up the atmosphere, it immerses you deeply into the game. The gameplay is solid, offering a nice blend of realism and excitement. The HypermotionV technology takes it up a notch, adding a cinematic flair to every move on the pitch. It's easy to pick up but offers enough depth to keep you engaged for hours, making it hard to master. The Ultimate Team feature, especially with its daily and weekly updates, provides endless fun and replayability. The atmosphere in the stadiums is spectacular, with crowd cheering that truly makes you feel like you're part of the action. As a newcomer to the series, I'm thoroughly satisfied with the experience.Cons:Unfortunately, the experience is marred by several issues. The EA app, a necessary evil, is riddled with bugs that often prevent smooth gameplay. It's frustrating to deal with constant crashes and the need to repeatedly download the app. The game lags during cutscenes, disrupting the flow of the narrative. Online matches, even with friends, suffer from lag issues, indicating a need for better optimization. The navigation menu, particularly with controller inputs, is a headache, as it frequently becomes unresponsive, hindering the overall experience.Overall:EA FC Sports 24 has all the ingredients for an exceptional gaming experience, but its potential is hampered by technical issues. Despite its flaws, the game shines in many aspects, offering thrilling gameplay and immersive features. With some much-needed fixes and optimizations, it could easily become the ultimate sports gaming experience.

I bought this game for an 80% discount, around $15. So keep that in mind. I have not played FIFA in a while, probably since 2022. This is my review after coming back to the franchise from a break.1) GAMEPLAYCompared to some of their previous titles, FC24 is a bit clunky, doesn't move as smooth as 2018 or 2022 used to feel. This might be a matter of how much optimization you're able to achieve on your specific system by adjusting the settings as well. Unfortunately this can only take you so far. The studio needs to put more effort into optimizing performance and improving gameplay, especially online gameplay.2) VISUALSPretty much the same as the previous titles, save some small tweaks and improvements that might make the players look more realistic. Sometimes the crowd glitches out and appears to have no textures in cutscenes.3) AUDIOThe audio selection is always pretty good in FIFA, and the choice of menu songs gives a sense of nostalgia that no other EA Sports game has. As for gameplay audio, everything is pretty much the same as FIFA 22.4) PLAYERSThe rosters are updated and accurate. The stats for the players are adjusted according to their performance in the real game.5) GAMEMODESExact same stuff as FIFA 22. I quite enjoyed playing Volta with a couple of friends on LAN. It actually feels smoother and better in terms of gameplay than the standard games. That's probably because the engine doesn't have to render as much stuff. Ultimate Team is always fun, however microtransctions have fully engulfed it now, just as it has in previous years. And if I'm not mistaken, FIFA is the most lucrative/profitable IP for EA...wonder why.6) MENUS/INTERFACEPretty clean and sleek, similar to previous games. I think the UI Team did a great job on this.OVERALL FC24 definitely took a hit on performance from previous years, probably from all the new stuff they've been adding. It has a similar vibe to previous years, so if you like a casual game to kick back and chill, this is not bad.

I'm gonna say this, and I need everyone to promise not to hurt me when I do...But uh, Fifa is fun again?I know, I know, blasphemy. Its not as good as it could be, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if FC24 hasn't held me, and its *especially* worth trying at 14 bucks on sale like I got it. I wish there was less MTX with that mode but thats a long lost battle at this point.What IS worth paying attention to is whats there beyond UT, and by that I mean career modes. I have a player career as a CM for the Spurs looking to trade into my longtime favorite team, Chelsea (woot woot) and I took over QPR as a manager and I mean... maybe its just me but the management mode is just super fun now? I really enjoy all the visuals and upgrades that have from when I last tried Fifa in 2021 when it was still called Fifa, but its such a jam piloting the day to day and matchday of a tier 2 English club. I'm an old PES player. Growing up, I had played PES (and winning 11 before that) for more than 10 years. But PES is no more. So I switched to FIFA since FIFA 23. And here is what I think.EA FC has more ways to play--different modes, online games, lotteries, etc, which kept me captivated. However, when it comes to capturing the feeling and experience of a soccer/football game, I think EA falls short in this regard. There seems to be only a handful way of playing it, of optimal formations, and ways to score goals. Just look at the online games, almost everybody uses the same formation. And it becomes a game that heavily relies on reaction time and muscle memory. If you want to get creative with how your team is set up, and what tactics to use, or just maybe an unexpected way to create a chance, you are not allowed to do so in most cases. The experience of actually playing a game quickly becomes very monolithic and it feels like there is only one correct way to play it.Secondly, I don't think EA successfully reproduces the distinctive style of real players. When I played PES, especially earlier ones, when you control a certain player in the game, it feels like it is really that player you are using. In EA FC, however, the difference between players are only reflected in their how fast they run, how strong they are, and how rapid their dribbles are, etc.. The difference is mostly physical and not stylistic.It's so sad to see that PES is over. But what can you do. My EA FC 24 has finished downloading on my new PC. I'm playing it.

Easily the worst FIFA game to dateThis review has been a long time brewing and is just a way for me to vent about how trash this game is. EA really need to stop releasing FIFA/FC games annually because they clearly can't do it. The amount of mistakes made weekly, maybe even daily is actually incredible. The teams people are rocking with now MIGHT be an end game team in some FIFAs. I remember FIFA 13/14 I was still rocking around with gold players at TOTS. The fact that promo cards are so common means they don't hold any value. It used to be very hype getting an inform card, let alone any other promo card, but now unless you get one of the bigger players, it's very much who cares.Evolutions could have been a saving grace, but they ruined that too. First season in the EPL I finish 7th, then next season I win the EPL and the conference League. All that in just 4 season, imagine if that was in real life, the team would build a statue and let the manager stay forever. 5th season, I sign Jude Bellingham in the first few days of the season. It ticks a box for a young player (24 years old) and then my manager level goes to red out of nowhere (remember I won 2 cups the previous season), I get sacked... for signing the best midfielder in the game.... It's incredible. What's the point of putting all this time into career mode when you get sacked for winning trophies and signing players? For memes I simmed the season as Boro (got sacked again btw) then as Forest, Preston with this superteam without me finished 6th... LOLInconsistent and not fun. Just feels like a chore to play. Prawn stir-fryIngredients:200g raw, peeled tiger prawns from a sustainable source1 green Thai chilli, chopped3 garlic cloves, 1 crushed and 2 finely sliced1 bunch coriander, leaves and stalks separated1 tbsp caster sugarjuice 1 lime3 tbsp fish sauce2 tbsp groundnut oil3cm piece ginger, finely sliced, then shredded8 spring onions, finely sliced1 red pepper, thinly sliced85g water chestnuts, sliced100g beansprouts1 tbsp soy sauceegg or rice noodles, to servelime wedges, to serveSTEP 1Put the prawns in a bowl. Put the chilli, garlic, coriander stalks (snip these up using scissors first) and caster sugar in a spice grinder or small food processor and whizz together. Add half of the lime juice and the fish sauce, then pour this over the prawns.STEP 2Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok, add the ginger and spring onions and fry for 1 min. Add the red pepper and fry for 1 min, until the pepper starts to soften. Add the water chestnuts and bean sprouts, and toss together until the bean sprouts start to wilt. Add the soy sauce and a really good grind of black pepper, then tip the lot into a serving dish.STEP 3Heat the remaining oil in the wok and add the prawns, lifting them out of their juices. Toss for 1-2 mins until they turn pink, add the marinade and swirl the wok quickly, then tip the lot onto the veg. Snip over the coriander leaves and sprinkle on the remaining lime. Serves over noodles with extra lime for squeezing over.

This review covers strictly the online game play portion of the game.EA FC 24 is, in short, the accumulation of many positives and negatives of the last few years of FIFA. I grew up playing FIFA 08-17, and in this time, I truly believe the game was at its best. Though graphics and physics weren't perfect, they had this element of true-to-skill game-play. From shooting to passing to defense, it all required specifically timed inputs to perform successfully. What I have noticed about new EA Sports games is that their best way to smooth out visible glitches and errors was to switch to an animation system. I call it an animation system because the game seems to follow a loosely pre-planned course that players can, from time to time, increase their likelihood that the animations being shown to them are in their favor.As many players have noticed, the so-called "bounce-back system" is a feature that seems to allow certain players (even me, I promise I'm not just crying) to have on the ball advantages and higher rebound potential. Usually in the closing minutes of the game or right after the opposition has scored, the bounce-back system guides one squad to a goal, seemingly to create a closer and more exciting game.Through all my years of playing sports games and hearing "EA Sports games are scripted" I am finally giving in and agreeing. I have truly begun to believe that the game follows a pre-determined timeline. Maybe not determining a winner before the game starts, but at least guiding the game into a direction it would previously not have gone.To conclude, I want to say that FC 24 is, in my opinion worse than the last 3 years of FIFA. Pack luck and RGN is no longer a concern of mine as I bought this game knowing I would be disappointed by those things. Content is constantly added that keeps me coming back to the game months after release. I have no where near the amount of hours on FC 24 as I did on FIFA(s) 21-23. Good luck next year EA! :)

The game itself slows in its improvement more and more each year and for me, the gameplay took a major regression after FIFA 17/18.I wish I could enjoy this game, but I just can't realistically do so. The use of advantage is terrible - sometimes not triggering at all, sometimes triggering when the advantage is actually being played, sometimes triggering way way too late, after the attacking team has already made an unsuccessful attempt at the goal. I have both suffered and benefited from situations in which:- a throw-in was dictated despite the ball not leaving the pitch, not even touching the by-line- a penalty was awarded without one player touching another- a red card was given without an actual foul being committedand many others.Second off, the input is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ in some way. Only reason I'm giving this game a positive review is because I personally had a lot of fun in it. I have not played FIFA 23 much, but from everything I have seen and heard previously, it's pretty much just a retexture of the previous one.Was not the biggest fan of Ultimate Team past 2017, so I can't say if it's any better or worse in that regard but the career mode is alright, I'd say. I like some of the new mechanics that were implemented, but they're nothing massive by any means. At it's core it's just classic career mode, with a few new options. The cutscenes haven't changed at all, the way transfers work is mostly the same and certain aspects are completely broken. The broken and OP things aren't too much of an issue in my opinion, seeing as you don't encounter these things 90% of the time, but if they bother you that much, you can always download a few realism and bug-fix mods, if you have the time.With all that being said, I can recommend the game but only if it's on sale, and you don't already own FIFA 23.

EA have dropped the FIFA moniker after losing the naming rights and are now presenting their premier football franchise with a fresh look. Players move behind their markers consistently leading to needlessly lost possession, passes often lead to nothing, it takes an absurd amount of time to even get your FUT squad even to 86 unless you buy coins or points and any other modes besides FUT and Career Mode are akin to huffing pure carbon monoxide.PROSMenus look really nice, bugs aside. The redesign feels very fresh and clean, and the menus are newly optimised for lower end hardware in comparison to FIFA 23. Mods, as usual, heavily carry this game just like any other FIFA franchise game on PC. FIFER, RODE, WZRD and the eSIM projects are all worth looking into this year just like any other year and they all deliver well. The game has FAR better performance than 23 and even 22, leading to being able to run this on anything from lower mid end to the upper echelons of PC builds. Career mode feels roughly the same as 23, but that's not to discredit the mode. It still delivers (as long as you use mods) just like any other variant of it and there's lots of room for creativity. I haven't played Pro Clubs as of yet but I assume it offers much of the same as it always has, same goes for VOLTA this year.THE VERDICTUse the Anadius Denuvo workaround to play this game until you're 100% sure you want it, the gameplay is different enough from 23 for this to be kind of a neccessity. It runs far better than 23 but it still can have performance issues on very low end hardware. And of course, modding is the way to go as always.

Suddenly, players move like they're carrying the weight of the world on their shoulders. It's like they're auditioning for a slow-motion ballet instead of playing a football game. Passing, tackles, and rebounds? Ah, who needs logical game mechanics when you can have chaos that feels completely AI-controlled?In conclusion, FC24 is a masterpiece if you consider "masterpiece" to be a synonym for disaster. Save your money, buy a bag of popcorn, and watch turtle races instead – at least you'll get more excitement and a better return on your investment. L'altre dia revisant la nova aplicació d'EA per escriptori em vaig informar que hi havia jugat 1008 hores. És un joc que tot i allunyar-se bastant de la simulació i apropar-se molt més a l' em divertia prou com per seguir jugant a estones.L'EA FC 24 em sembla una evolució d'aquell joc. I això no és necessàriament quelcom positiu. Han passat bastants anys, i és en essència el mateix joc, però m'ha resultat molt menys divertit. Hi he detectat moltes més animacions. D'algunes curioses com que els jugadors es col·loquen les mans al darrere automàticament quan defensen dins de l'àrea, que ajuden a millorar la versemblança amb la realitat. D'altres amb una intenció, entenc que més pràctica com les diferents formes d'acompanyar la pilota amb els peus mentre s'avança ja sigui caminant o corrents. Però de fet, no aporten canvis substancials.El joc continua sent totalment , fins al punt que em sembla encara més que a l'edició anterior que havia jugat. És molt difícil simular el futbol real, moure la pilota correctament, fer la passada en el moment correcte de la desmarcada, etc. perquè al meu parer la intel·ligència dels jugadors del mateix equip no controlats per l'usuari no actua simulant la realitat en dificultats mitjanes. A més a més en dificultats elevades els rivals, l'equip no controlat pel jugador, son completament perfectes i en dificultats inferiors simplement no competeixen, van caminant pel camp badant boca.Tot i provar les diferents tàctiques de plantilla que ofereix el joc, un cop al camp les diferències són ridícules. Els davanters queden totalment en línia amb els defenses sense oferir desmarcades, el migcamp no es mou i els defenses actuen de manera automàtica. Defensar és complicat i requereix d'una precisió incòmode ja que la càmera és massa lluny de l'acció, i ho ha de ser per poder veure tot el camp, canviar a una càmera més propera, fa que es perdi el joc tàctic per la visió reduïda, i tampoc millora massa l'habilitat defensiva. Caldria replantejar, al meu parer, la interacció necessària del jugador perquè senti diversió enlloc de frustració a l'hora de defensar.Penso també que el joc està excessivament pre-configurat o automatitzat. Les accions del joc no son el resultat d'una simulació lliure sinó que tenen paràmetres (interns, amagats darrere de línies de codi) que controlen les possibilitats de manera, al meu parer, artificial. Això fa que en ocasions sigui frustrant jugar-hi i per tant redueix forçosament la diversió. Així com també genera situacions absurdes o injustes. Jugadors ràpids que van lents, jugadors amb menys massa muscular que d'altres que guanyen xocs físics sense problemes, jugadors baixos amb poc salt que guanyen de cap a jugadors més alts i forts, etc. No és la norma, però tampoc l'excepció, ocorre més sovint del que pot semblar. He de suposar que la raó no és manipular als jugadors per a que acabin prenent segons quines decisions ja que les coses no surten com la majoria s'esperaria al camp, sinó un desenvolupament maldestre. Sigui quina sigui la opció, l'empresa no queda gens ben parada.Podria seguir parlant del joc sobre el camp en sí, però sento que no acabaria mai així que seguiré amb un breu comentari sobre tot el que hi al voltant.En resum: És lamentable. Fa vergonya.Modes de joc completament enfocats a que infants i joves dediquin el temps a apostes encobertes amb guanys ínfims i ridículs en una espiral d'addicció que pot arribar a provocar traumes, entre d'altres patologies greus. I tot gràcies al sistema capitalisme en el que vivim actualment. Només fa ganes de vomitar. Modes de joc com el mode de carrera o d'altres continuen amb el nucli igual que al FIFA 18, amb petites adicions que al meu entendre, el tornen més feixuc enlloc de més divertit. I comentar que continua la norma de que els jugadors menors de 17 anys no són al joc i que no tots els equips compten amb llicència oficial, destacant sobretot equips italians.Finalment dir que el primer que vaig intentar fer un cop el joc havia acabat d'instal·lar-se és jugar una temporada de amb el F.C. Barcelona d'enguany (2023/24), ja que sóc soci del club i encara hem de competir en aquesta Lliga del règim a falta de lliga Catalana oficial. Bé doncs, la meva sorpresa fou que no és possible. Només s'hi poden fer competicions (no estic parlant del mode carrera) amb les plantilles de l'any anterior, però no de l'actual. La decepció va ser gegant, però tot i així, vaig aguantar i vaig dedicar-li unes hores més. Hores avorrides i perdudes.L'única cosa positiva que n'he tret és que m'ha fet cercar alguna alternativa vàlida i l'he trobat. Es diu Football Life 2024, una versió molt adaptada, actualitzada i millorada del Pro Evolution Soccer 2021. Una iniciativa d'un entusiasta de Palestina/Jordania que amb un grup de persones d'arreu han aconseguit oferir una gran alternativa als que ens divertim simulant el futbol de manera digital.
