Tried this out on the free weekend. It's a nice game but I'm not sure if it's the game for me.Graphically, it's a beautiful game with realistic looking players, fans, stadiums, etc. Top notch visual realism despite the occasional quirks like players sometimes celebrating near other players or objects and seeing their arms/legs being unnaturally bent in odd shapes or directions. That you can customize the look of your manager is a nice touch.Gameplay, I came into this hoping that it had a deep managerial side to the game. I just want to dictate the orders and strategies and then let the players implement the game plan as best as they can. I don't like having to control and influence players through the use of a controller, to me that defeats the purpose of being a Manager. However, that's how it defaults you. BUT, you can switch to Tactical View of the game and watch from the Manager's sideline box or switch to a spectator cam for a tv-style ease of viewing. In that you can definitely be a Manager and bark instructions to the team via keyboard commands, again I dislike using a controller as a Manager. As far as the gameplay as a player, I didn't do much of it but it seems to be somewhat intuitive though the differences between kicking and passing aren't as easy to grasp as even using the pass button on my mouse will sometimes send the ball far out of play. It takes some getting used to as far as dragging the line to tell your player which direction to run, etc. Overall, for this mode of gameplay I suppose it's fine. But I wanted to play the game as a footy manager. Controller players who will want to control the players themselves should find this mode joyful.Depth of the game was a bit disappointing. I fully realize that there is Licensing involved as I play a fair bit of other sports manager games and they all have their quirks with feeling incomplete. This game is no exception. While I was excited to see women's leagues in the game, I was disappointed there was no Manager mode for the women. Oddly, even though I can manage men's teams in mode outside of managerial career, such as setting up a custom tournament... I was unable to do that with the women's teams. Very disappointed with that. And while I was surprised to see small footy leagues like Norway's in the game, I was shocked that Mexico's league wasn't in the game. How then can they justify having national teams for countries who don't have their leagues in the game and with no national player pool to draw from while at the same time claiming you cannot add women's management because there's not enough of a national player pool for the women? That reeks of both bias and sexism.Overall, I think this is an alright game. It's not the best, yet it's certainly not the worst. I would say this is near the top and if improved upon could be the best. I had fun trying it out this weekend and I'm still up in the air as to whether I will buy it or wait and see if FC 25 improves upon this and adds women's management plus more international leagues and competitions for both the men and women as well as a deeper managerial career in terms of expanding on what's here with more leagues, teams and competitions. For what is here, it's still a good game. But I want total football and total control with the ability to coach any gender in any part of the world whether it's China, Chile, or Chicago. I want it all.For players who enjoy player career modes, this is your game. From what I saw of playing around with it, it looks fantastic for that. For players who want footy manager sim game, there's enough here to give you a lot of enjoyment but you may come away feeling it's a little incomplete or lacking in depth in some areas. Still, I recommend this game because it's the closest we'll get for now to a marriage of a football manager game with phenomenal graphics.Other reviewers are right, EA gets a lot of hate. Some of it unjustified. I'm an old-timer who remembers when EA was on 5.25" floppy discs as an Indie publisher helping Indie developers make a name for themselves. They've done a lot for the video game genre and while they've had their shortcomings over the years, I don't see it as being necessary to treat them so harshly when other companies do far, far worse. Besides, there's already enough hate and meanness in this world without my adding to it.Peace out.

It feels like they only care about graphics, collectibles and customization. eFootball is way better.I played FIFA from 2002 to FIFA 18 and then I said enough is enough. I only tried 19, 20, 21, 22 and 23 during free weekends or free trials and each time I was glad I switched to PES. Playing co-op with friends in PES 2020 and 2021 was the most fun I had in football games for a very long time.FIFA Pro Clubs were also pretty fun, but it was always difficult to gather a full 11 people squad, so if we didn't have enough and opponents had a full team, we didn't stand a chance.As for what we play nowadays - eFootball finally added co-op events with matchmaking pretty recently and it's what we play the most. You can play 2v2 or 3v3 using your cards (like from FUT) and the games takes 11-12 cards from each player for 2v2 or 7-8 cards for 3v3. The party leader chooses squad and tactics from all players' cards in the lobby (Game Plan) before the start of the match, so it's really fun to play with your friends' cards.What's also great about eFootball, all cards carryover to the next season. The game gets updated, you get new gameplay and graphics and you can still play with your favourite players. In FIFA/EA FC when you spend real money on cards, it's gone when the new game launches. In eFootball you get to keep everything (players contracts expire after 365 days, but you can extend them for GP points you get just from playing, I always have way more GP than I need).And finally, the gameplay is way better in eFootball. I recommend turning down passing assist to PA3 (PA4 is full manual). You have more control of your passes, the ball goes more in the direction you want instead of where the assist wants it to, and it's still slightly assited, so you don't need to set the power and direction perfectly. It gets some time to get used to, but it's well worth it.Oh, and eFootball is free, I play it since 2021 and I spent only 2€ on coins so far (I wanted specific Zieliński card from a pack and I didn't want to grind for coins then), and from free spins and other gifts or events I already have more legends than space in squad and bench (you can have 23 players in your roster - I have more legends than that for free).
